title: How can watermarks be embedded in text generated by LLMs?
question: This is a follow-up to the following question: How can I remove text watermarks from Claude output? I didn't fully understand that question or the discussion in the comments, so I would like to know how watermarks are technically embedded in the text generated by LLMs. What are the possible mechanisms or methods to achieve this?
answer: If you want to embed watermarks in your text generated by LLMs, there are three basic categories of methods: 1. The visible text itself Words Sentence structure Style Punctuation Word/order sequence Statistical properties 2. The character sequence underlying the visible representation Unicode variants Invisible characters Whitespace Control characters Homoglyphs Normalization variants 3. Information outside the actual text Metadata File information Cryptographic signatures The following are ways someone could try to circumvent or neutralize these different types of watermarking: 1. The visible text itself Write/review the text yourself Use your own wording and structure Avoid relying on automated rewriting Verify the content independently 2. The character sequence underlying the visible representation Normalize the text to a standard Unicode form Remove non-printing/control characters Validate and sanitize the character set Convert the text to a clean plain-text representation 3. Information outside the actual text Inspect metadata before sharing Remove unnecessary metadata Export the content as clean plain text when appropriate Check files for embedded provenance information I think the following are the most relevant classes when it comes to watermarking, labeling, marking, disclosure, or identification of text generated by LLMs, based on this post: How can I remove text wat...
